Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# The Silver Searcher

A code searching tool similar to `ack`, with a focus on speed.

## What's so great about Ag?

* It is an order of magnitude faster than `ack`.
* It ignores file patterns from your `.gitignore` and `.hgignore`.
* If there are files in your source repo you don't want to search, just add their patterns to a `.ignore` file. (\*cough\* `*.min.js` \*cough\*)
* The command name is 33% shorter than `ack`, and all keys are on the home row!

Ag is quite stable now. Most changes are new features, minor bug fixes, or performance improvements. It's much faster than Ack in my benchmarks:

    ack test_blah ~/code/  104.66s user 4.82s system 99% cpu 1:50.03 total

    ag test_blah ~/code/  4.67s user 4.58s system 286% cpu 3.227 total

Ack and Ag found the same results, but Ag was 34x faster (3.2 seconds vs 110 seconds). My `~/code` directory is about 8GB. Thanks to git/hg/ignore, Ag only searched 700MB of that.

## Installing

### macOS

    brew install the_silver_searcher

or

    port install the_silver_searcher


### Linux

* Ubuntu >= 13.10 (Saucy) or Debian >= 8 (Jessie)

        apt-get install silversearcher-ag
* Fedora 21 and lower

        yum install the_silver_searcher
* Fedora 22+

        dnf install the_silver_searcher
* RHEL7+

        yum install epel-release.noarch the_silver_searcher
* Gentoo

        emerge -a sys-apps/the_silver_searcher
* Arch

        pacman -S the_silver_searcher

* Slackware

        sbopkg -i the_silver_searcher

* openSUSE

        zypper install the_silver_searcher

* CentOS

        yum install the_silver_searcher

* NixOS/Nix/Nixpkgs

        nix-env -iA silver-searcher

* SUSE Linux Enterprise: Follow [these simple instructions](https://software.opensuse.org/download.html?project=utilities&package=the_silver_searcher).


### BSD

* FreeBSD

        pkg install the_silver_searcher
* OpenBSD/NetBSD

        pkg_add the_silver_searcher

### Windows

* Win32/64

  Unofficial daily builds are [available](https://github.com/k-takata/the_silver_searcher-win32).
  
* winget

        winget install "The Silver Searcher"
  
  Notes:
  - This installs a [release](https://github.com/JFLarvoire/the_silver_searcher/releases) of ag.exe optimized for Windows.
  - winget is intended to become the default package manager client for Windows.  
    As of June 2020, it's still in beta, and can be installed using instructions [there](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-cli).
  - The setup script in the Ag's winget package installs ag.exe in the first directory that matches one of these criteria:
     1. Over a previous instance of ag.exe *from the same [origin](https://github.com/JFLarvoire/the_silver_searcher)* found in the PATH
     2. In the directory defined in environment variable bindir_%PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE%
     3. In the directory defined in environment variable bindir
     4. In the directory defined in environment variable windir
  
* Chocolatey

        choco install ag
* MSYS2

        pacman -S mingw-w64-{i686,x86_64}-ag
* Cygwin

  Run the relevant [`setup-*.exe`](https://cygwin.com/install.html), and select "the\_silver\_searcher" in the "Utils" category.

## Editor Integration

### Vim

You can use Ag with [ack.vim](https://github.com/mileszs/ack.vim) by adding the following line to your `.vimrc`:

    let g:ackprg = 'ag --nogroup --nocolor --column'

or:

    let g:ackprg = 'ag --vimgrep'

Which has the same effect but will report every match on the line.

### Emacs

You can use [ag.el][] as an Emacs front-end to Ag. See also: [helm-ag].

[ag.el]: https://github.com/Wilfred/ag.el
[helm-ag]: https://github.com/syohex/emacs-helm-ag

### TextMate

TextMate users can use Ag with [my fork](https://github.com/ggreer/AckMate) of the popular AckMate plugin, which lets you use both Ack and Ag for searching. If you already have AckMate you just want to replace Ack with Ag, move or delete `"~/Library/Application Support/TextMate/PlugIns/AckMate.tmplugin/Contents/Resources/ackmate_ack"` and run `ln -s /usr/local/bin/ag "~/Library/Application Support/TextMate/PlugIns/AckMate.tmplugin/Contents/Resources/ackmate_ack"`

## Other stuff you might like

* [Ack](https://github.com/petdance/ack3) - Better than grep. Without Ack, Ag would not exist.
* [ack.vim](https://github.com/mileszs/ack.vim)
* [Exuberant Ctags](http://ctags.sourceforge.net/) - Faster than Ag, but it builds an index beforehand. Good for *really* big codebases.
* [Git-grep](http://git-scm.com/docs/git-grep) - As fast as Ag but only works on git repos.
* [fzf](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf) - A command-line fuzzy finder 
* [ripgrep](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep)
* [Sack](https://github.com/sampson-chen/sack) - A utility that wraps Ack and Ag. It removes a lot of repetition from searching and opening matching files.

## Documentation

For detailed usage information and command-line options, see the manual page in the `doc/` directory.

"""Behavioral regression tests; these do not need the observation executable."""
import gzip
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

EXE = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'executable')


class SearchTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.temp.name)
        self.write('a.txt', b'zero\nFoo foo food FOO\nnone\nfoo\nlast\n')
        self.write('b.py', b'foo bar\nother\nFOO\n')
        self.write('none', b'nothing\n')
        self.write('empty', b'')
        self.write('sub/c.txt', b'foo sub\n')
        self.write('.hidden', b'foo hidden\n')
        self.write('binary', b'before\0foo after\n')

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temp.cleanup()

    def write(self, name, contents):
        path = self.root / name
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_bytes(contents)

    def command(self, *args, data=None):
        return subprocess.run([EXE, '--workers=1', *args], cwd=self.root,
                              stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL if data is None else None,
                              input=data, capture_output=True, timeout=5)

    def check(self, args, output, code=0, error=b'', data=None):
        p = self.command(*args, data=data)
        self.assertEqual((p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr), (code, output, error))

    def test_smart_case(self):
        self.check(['foo', 'a.txt'], b'2:Foo foo food FOO\n4:foo\n')
        self.check(['Foo', 'a.txt'], b'2:Foo foo food FOO\n')
        self.check(['-s', '-c', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'3\n')
        self.check(['-i', '-c', 'FOO', 'a.txt'], b'5\n')

    def test_literal_and_word_matching(self):
        self.check(['-w', '-c', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'4\n')
        self.check(['-Q', 'foo|bar', 'b.py'], b'', code=1)
        self.check(['-c', 'foo|bar', 'b.py'], b'3\n')
        self.check(['-o', '(?<=foo )food', 'a.txt'], b'food\n')

    def test_paths_and_grouping(self):
        self.check(['--heading', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'a.txt\n2:Foo foo food FOO\n4:foo\n')
        self.check(['--noheading', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'a.txt:2:Foo foo food FOO\na.txt:4:foo\n')
        self.check(['--group', 'foo', 'a.txt', 'b.py'],
                   b'a.txt\n2:Foo foo food FOO\n4:foo\n\nb.py\n1:foo bar\n3:FOO\n')
        self.check(['--nofilename', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'Foo foo food FOO\nfoo\n')

    def test_recursive_search(self):
        self.check(['-g', r'\.txt$', '.'], b'sub/c.txt\na.txt\n')
        self.check(['-n', '-g', r'\.txt$', '.'], b'a.txt\n')
        self.check(['--python', 'foo', '.'], b'b.py:1:foo bar\nb.py:3:FOO\n')
        self.check(['-G', r'\.py$', 'foo', '.'], b'b.py:1:foo bar\nb.py:3:FOO\n')

    def test_only_matching(self):
        self.check(['-o', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'Foo\nfoo\nfoo\nFOO\nfoo\n')
        self.check(['-o', '--column', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'1:Foo\n5:foo\n9:foo\n14:FOO\n1:foo\n')
        self.check(['-o', '--numbers', 'foo'], b'1:foo\n1:foo\n', data=b'foo foo\n')

    def test_counts_and_filenames(self):
        self.check(['-c', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'5\n')
        self.check(['-c', 'foo', 'none'], b'', code=1)
        self.check(['-l', '-0', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'a.txt\0')
        self.check(['-L', 'foo', 'none'], b'none\n')
        self.check(['-L', 'foo', 'empty'], b'', code=1)
        self.check(['--print-all-files', '-c', 'foo', 'none'], b'0\n')

    def test_context(self):
        self.write('context', b'one\ntwo\nfoo\nfour\nfive\nsix\nfoo\neight\n')
        self.check(['-C1', 'foo', 'context'], b'2-two\n3:foo\n4-four\n--\n6-six\n7:foo\n8-eight\n')
        self.check(['-A2', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'2:Foo foo food FOO\n3-none\n4:foo\n5-last\n6-\n')
        self.check(['-C1', '--column', 'foo', 'context'],
                   b'2-two\n3:1:foo\n4-four\n--\n6-six\n7:1:foo\n8-eight\n')

    def test_inversion(self):
        self.check(['-v', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'1:zero\n3:none\n5:last\n')
        self.check(['-v', '-c', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'3\n')
        self.check(['-v', '-c', 'absent', 'a.txt'], b'1\n')
        self.check(['-v', 'foo'], b'zero\nlast', data=b'zero\nfoo\nlast')

    def test_stream(self):
        self.check(['foo'], b'foo foo\nfoo', data=b'none\nfoo foo\nfoo')
        self.check(['-c', 'foo'], b'2\n1\n', data=b'none\nfoo foo\nfoo')
        self.check(['--numbers', 'foo'], b'2:foo\n', data=b'none\nfoo\n')
        self.check(['--passthrough', '--numbers', 'foo'], b'none\n2:foo\nlast', data=b'none\nfoo\nlast')
        self.check(['foo', 'a.txt'], b'Foo foo food FOO\nfoo\n', data=b'other input')

    def test_binary(self):
        self.check(['foo', 'binary'], b'', code=1)
        self.check(['--search-binary', 'foo', 'binary'], b'Binary file binary matches.\n')
        self.check(['-a', '-c', 'foo', 'binary'], b'1\n')

    def test_ignores(self):
        self.write('.gitignore', b'*.txt\n!c.txt\n')
        self.check(['-g', r'\.txt$', '.'], b'sub/c.txt\n')
        self.check(['-U', '-g', r'\.txt$', '.'], b'sub/c.txt\na.txt\n')
        self.check(['--ignore', 'sub', '-g', r'\.txt$', '.'], b'', code=1)
        self.check(['foo', 'a.txt'], b'2:Foo foo food FOO\n4:foo\n')
        self.write('sub/.ignore', b'!a.txt\n')
        self.write('sub/a.txt', b'foo\n')
        self.check(['-g', 'sub/a.txt', '.'], b'', code=1)
        self.check(['-g', 'a.txt', 'sub'], b'sub/a.txt\n')

    def test_editor_formats(self):
        self.check(['--ackmate', 'foo', 'b.py'], b'1;0 3:foo bar\n3;0 3:FOO\n')
        self.check(['--vimgrep', 'foo', 'b.py'], b'b.py:1:1:foo bar\nb.py:3:1:FOO\n')
        self.check(['--nonumbers', '--vimgrep', 'foo', 'b.py'], b'b.py:1:foo bar\nb.py:1:FOO\n')

    def test_multiline_and_empty_matches(self):
        self.write('multiline', b'foo\nabc\ndef\n')
        self.check([r'foo\nabc', 'multiline'], b'1:foo\n2:abc\n')
        self.check(['--column', r'foo\nabc', 'multiline'], b'1:1:foo\n2:0:abc\n')
        self.check(['--nomultiline', r'foo\nabc', 'multiline'], b'', code=1)
        self.check(['.*', 'multiline'], b'1:foo\n')
        self.check(['-c', '.*', 'multiline'], b'6\n')
        self.check(['-o', '^', 'multiline'], b'\n\n\n')

    def test_colors(self):
        reset = b'\x1b[0m\x1b[K'
        self.check(['--color', 'foo'], b'\x1b[30;43mfoo' + reset + b'\n', data=b'foo\n')
        self.check(['--color', '-c', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'\x1b[1;33m5' + reset + b'\n')

    def test_width_and_limit(self):
        self.check(['-W6', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'2:Foo fo [...]\n4:foo\n')
        self.check(['-m1', '-c', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'1\n',
                   error=b'ERR: Too many matches in a.txt. Skipping the rest of this file.\n')
        self.check(['--silent', '-m1', '-c', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'1\n')

    def test_compressed(self):
        self.write('packed.gz', gzip.compress(b'foo\nnone\nfoo\n'))
        self.check(['-z', 'foo', 'packed.gz'], b'1:foo\n4:')
        self.check(['-z', '-c', 'foo', 'packed.gz'], b'1\n1\n')

    def test_errors(self):
        self.check(['--width=bad', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'', code=2, error=b'ERR: Invalid width\n\n')
        self.check(['[', 'a.txt'], b'', code=2,
                   error=b'ERR: Bad regex! pcre_compile() failed at position 1: missing terminating ] for character class\nIf you meant to search for a literal string, run ag with -Q\n')
        self.check(['foo', 'missing'], b'', code=1,
                   error=b'ERR: Error stat()ing: missing\nERR: Error opening directory missing: No such file or directory\n')
        self.check(['--silent', 'foo', 'missing'], b'', code=1)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

# Building and testing

Run `./compile.sh` from a checkout to create `./executable`. The build uses
Python 3's standard-library zipapp builder and does not download packages.
The generated application bundles all of its Python modules and can be run
from any working directory.

The search engine uses the generic system PCRE runtime when available, with
a standard-library regular-expression fallback. It does not invoke another
search program. Gzip and xz decompression use Python's standard library.

Run the regression suite after building:

```
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The implementation separates CLI parsing, byte-oriented matching, directory
traversal and ignore handling, and result rendering. The tests use isolated
temporary directories and cover streams, recursive searches, filename filters,
context, count/list modes, editor formats, colors, binary files, compressed
files, and error handling. Build outputs and caches are ignored by Git.

python3 -m zipapp build/package -p '/usr/bin/env python3' -o executable
chmod +x executable
EOF

"""Behavioral regression tests; these do not need the observation executable."""
import gzip
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

EXE = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'executable')


class SearchTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.temp.name)
        self.write('a.txt', b'zero\nFoo foo food FOO\nnone\nfoo\nlast\n')
        self.write('b.py', b'foo bar\nother\nFOO\n')
        self.write('none', b'nothing\n')
        self.write('empty', b'')
        self.write('sub/c.txt', b'foo sub\n')
        self.write('.hidden', b'foo hidden\n')
        self.write('binary', b'before\0foo after\n')

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temp.cleanup()

    def write(self, name, contents):
        path = self.root / name
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_bytes(contents)

    def command(self, *args, data=None):
        return subprocess.run([EXE, '--workers=1', *args], cwd=self.root,
                              stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL if data is None else None,
                              input=data, capture_output=True, timeout=5)

    def check(self, args, output, code=0, error=b'', data=None):
        p = self.command(*args, data=data)
        self.assertEqual((p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr), (code, output, error))

    def test_smart_case(self):
        self.check(['foo', 'a.txt'], b'2:Foo foo food FOO\n4:foo\n')
        self.check(['Foo', 'a.txt'], b'2:Foo foo food FOO\n')
        self.check(['-s', '-c', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'3\n')
        self.check(['-i', '-c', 'FOO', 'a.txt'], b'5\n')

    def test_literal_and_word_matching(self):
        self.check(['-w', '-c', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'4\n')
        self.check(['-Q', 'foo|bar', 'b.py'], b'', code=1)
        self.check(['-c', 'foo|bar', 'b.py'], b'3\n')
        self.check(['-o', '(?<=foo )food', 'a.txt'], b'food\n')

    def test_paths_and_grouping(self):
        self.check(['--heading', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'a.txt\n2:Foo foo food FOO\n4:foo\n')
        self.check(['--noheading', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'a.txt:2:Foo foo food FOO\na.txt:4:foo\n')
        self.check(['--group', 'foo', 'a.txt', 'b.py'],
                   b'a.txt\n2:Foo foo food FOO\n4:foo\n\nb.py\n1:foo bar\n3:FOO\n')
        self.check(['--nofilename', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'Foo foo food FOO\nfoo\n')

    def test_recursive_search(self):
        self.check(['-g', r'\.txt$', '.'], b'sub/c.txt\na.txt\n')
        self.check(['-n', '-g', r'\.txt$', '.'], b'a.txt\n')
        self.check(['--python', 'foo', '.'], b'b.py:1:foo bar\nb.py:3:FOO\n')
        self.check(['-G', r'\.py$', 'foo', '.'], b'b.py:1:foo bar\nb.py:3:FOO\n')

    def test_only_matching(self):
        self.check(['-o', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'Foo\nfoo\nfoo\nFOO\nfoo\n')
        self.check(['-o', '--column', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'1:Foo\n5:foo\n9:foo\n14:FOO\n1:foo\n')
        self.check(['-o', '--numbers', 'foo'], b'1:foo\n1:foo\n', data=b'foo foo\n')

    def test_counts_and_filenames(self):
        self.check(['-c', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'5\n')
        self.check(['-c', 'foo', 'none'], b'', code=1)
        self.check(['-l', '-0', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'a.txt\0')
        self.check(['-L', 'foo', 'none'], b'none\n')
        self.check(['-L', 'foo', 'empty'], b'', code=1)
        self.check(['--print-all-files', '-c', 'foo', 'none'], b'0\n')

    def test_context(self):
        self.write('context', b'one\ntwo\nfoo\nfour\nfive\nsix\nfoo\neight\n')
        self.check(['-C1', 'foo', 'context'], b'2-two\n3:foo\n4-four\n--\n6-six\n7:foo\n8-eight\n')
        self.check(['-A2', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'2:Foo foo food FOO\n3-none\n4:foo\n5-last\n6-\n')
        self.check(['-C1', '--column', 'foo', 'context'],
                   b'2-two\n3:1:foo\n4-four\n--\n6-six\n7:1:foo\n8-eight\n')

    def test_inversion(self):
        self.check(['-v', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'1:zero\n3:none\n5:last\n')
        self.check(['-v', '-c', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'3\n')
        self.check(['-v', '-c', 'absent', 'a.txt'], b'1\n')
        self.check(['-v', 'foo'], b'zero\nlast', data=b'zero\nfoo\nlast')

    def test_stream(self):
        self.check(['foo'], b'foo foo\nfoo', data=b'none\nfoo foo\nfoo')
        self.check(['-c', 'foo'], b'2\n1\n', data=b'none\nfoo foo\nfoo')
        self.check(['--numbers', 'foo'], b'2:foo\n', data=b'none\nfoo\n')
        self.check(['--passthrough', '--numbers', 'foo'], b'none\n2:foo\nlast', data=b'none\nfoo\nlast')
        self.check(['foo', 'a.txt'], b'Foo foo food FOO\nfoo\n', data=b'other input')

    def test_binary(self):
        self.check(['foo', 'binary'], b'', code=1)
        self.check(['--search-binary', 'foo', 'binary'], b'Binary file binary matches.\n')
        self.check(['-a', '-c', 'foo', 'binary'], b'1\n')

    def test_ignores(self):
        self.write('.gitignore', b'*.txt\n!c.txt\n')
        self.check(['-g', r'\.txt$', '.'], b'sub/c.txt\n')
        self.check(['-U', '-g', r'\.txt$', '.'], b'sub/c.txt\na.txt\n')
        self.check(['--ignore', 'sub', '-g', r'\.txt$', '.'], b'', code=1)
        self.check(['foo', 'a.txt'], b'2:Foo foo food FOO\n4:foo\n')
        self.write('sub/.ignore', b'!a.txt\n')
        self.write('sub/a.txt', b'foo\n')
        self.check(['-g', 'sub/a.txt', '.'], b'', code=1)
        self.check(['-g', 'a.txt', 'sub'], b'sub/a.txt\n')

    def test_editor_formats(self):
        self.check(['--ackmate', 'foo', 'b.py'], b'1;0 3:foo bar\n3;0 3:FOO\n')
        self.check(['--vimgrep', 'foo', 'b.py'], b'b.py:1:1:foo bar\nb.py:3:1:FOO\n')
        self.check(['--nonumbers', '--vimgrep', 'foo', 'b.py'], b'b.py:1:foo bar\nb.py:1:FOO\n')

    def test_multiline_and_empty_matches(self):
        self.write('multiline', b'foo\nabc\ndef\n')
        self.check([r'foo\nabc', 'multiline'], b'1:foo\n2:abc\n')
        self.check(['--column', r'foo\nabc', 'multiline'], b'1:1:foo\n2:0:abc\n')
        self.check(['--nomultiline', r'foo\nabc', 'multiline'], b'', code=1)
        self.check(['.*', 'multiline'], b'1:foo\n')
        self.check(['-c', '.*', 'multiline'], b'6\n')
        self.check(['-o', '^', 'multiline'], b'\n\n\n')

    def test_colors(self):
        reset = b'\x1b[0m\x1b[K'
        self.check(['--color', 'foo'], b'\x1b[30;43mfoo' + reset + b'\n', data=b'foo\n')
        self.check(['--color', '-c', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'\x1b[1;33m5' + reset + b'\n')

    def test_width_and_limit(self):
        self.check(['-W6', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'2:Foo fo [...]\n4:foo\n')
        self.check(['-m1', '-c', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'1\n',
                   error=b'ERR: Too many matches in a.txt. Skipping the rest of this file.\n')
        self.check(['--silent', '-m1', '-c', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'1\n')

    def test_compressed(self):
        self.write('packed.gz', gzip.compress(b'foo\nnone\nfoo\n'))
        self.check(['-z', 'foo', 'packed.gz'], b'1:foo\n4:')
        self.check(['-z', '-c', 'foo', 'packed.gz'], b'1\n1\n')

    def test_errors(self):
        self.check(['--width=bad', 'foo', 'a.txt'], b'', code=2, error=b'ERR: Invalid width\n\n')
        self.check(['[', 'a.txt'], b'', code=2,
                   error=b'ERR: Bad regex! pcre_compile() failed at position 1: missing terminating ] for character class\nIf you meant to search for a literal string, run ag with -Q\n')
        self.check(['foo', 'missing'], b'', code=1,
                   error=b'ERR: Error stat()ing: missing\nERR: Error opening directory missing: No such file or directory\n')
        self.check(['--silent', 'foo', 'missing'], b'', code=1)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
PY
cat > BUILDING.md <<'EOF'
# Building and testing

Run `./compile.sh` from a checkout to create `./executable`. The build uses
Python 3's standard-library zipapp builder and does not download packages.
The generated application bundles all of its Python modules and can be run
from any working directory.

The search engine uses the generic system PCRE runtime when available, with
a standard-library regular-expression fallback. It does not invoke another
search program. Gzip and xz decompression use Python's standard library.

Run the regression suite after building:

```
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The implementation separates CLI parsing, byte-oriented matching, directory
traversal and ignore handling, and result rendering. The tests use isolated
temporary directories and cover streams, recursive searches, filename filters,
context, count/list modes, editor formats, colors, binary files, compressed
files, and error handling. Build outputs and caches are ignored by Git.
EOF
cat > compile.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
# Only Python's standard-library build tools are required. No package downloads.
command -v python3 >/dev/null
mkdir -p build/package
cp search_tool.py build/package/__main__.py
cp interface.py build/package/interface.py
python3 -m zipapp build/package -p '/usr/bin/env python3' -o executable
chmod +x executable
EOF
chmod +x compile.sh
./compile.sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
